props.title: Date with an Angel

sections.content: Date with an Angel represents the peak of 1980s romantic fantasy comedies, following in the footsteps of Splash (1984) and preceding similar celestial romance films like Wings of Desire (1987). Starring Michael E. Knight and Emmanuelle Béart, this whimsical tale about an injured angel crashing into a mortal's swimming pool captures the era's fascination with supernatural romance. The film shares DNA with other '80s fantasy-romance hybrids like Mannequin (1987) and Earth Girls Are Easy (1988), where otherworldly beings encounter modern life with both comedic and romantic results.

sections.content: The film's exploration of divine intervention in earthly romance connects it to later works like City of Angels (1998) and Michael (1996). Director Jim Wynorski, better known for his B-movies, attempted to blend screwball comedy with ethereal romance, creating a unique entry in the celestial visitor genre. The movie's practical effects and makeup work on Béart's angel character exemplify the pre-CGI era's approach to depicting supernatural beings, similar to the techniques used in Starman (1984).

While critically dismissed upon release, Date with an Angel has gained a cult following for its quintessentially '80s approach to romantic fantasy. Its influence can be traced through later supernatural romance films like Meet Joe Black (1998) and even modern variations like The Shape of Water (2017), where otherworldly beings and humans forge unlikely romantic connections. sections.content: The film sits at an interesting crossroads between classic angel-themed movies like Heaven Can Wait (1978) and more contemporary takes like Dogma (1999). Its treatment of heavenly beings as romantic leads rather than purely spiritual guides marked a shift in how cinema portrayed celestial entities. This transformation continued through films like The Preacher's Wife (1996) and What Dreams May Come (1998), where the divine became increasingly personalized and romantic.
